prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that David O. McKay, Spencer W. Kimball or James E. Faust dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where David O. McKay, Spencer W. Kimball, or James E. Faust dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: David O. McKay dedicated Bern Switzerland (1955), London England and Hamilton New Zealand (1958), and Los Angeles and Oakland in the United States. Spencer W. Kimball dedicated Washington D.C. (1974), São Paulo Brazil (1978) and Tokyo Japan (1980). James E. Faust dedicated several temples in 2000, including in Mexico, Costa Rica and the United States.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: McKay: Los Angeles (1956), Oakland (1964). Kimball: Washington D.C. (1974), Seattle (1980), rededications of St. George, Mesa, Laie and Logan. Faust: Medford, Memphis, Nashville, Oklahoma City (2000), Boise rededication (1987).

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Kimball: São Paulo Brazil (1978).

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Faust: Oaxaca Mexico and Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mexico (2000).

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: McKay: London England (1958).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Kimball: Tokyo Japan (1980).

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: McKay: Hamilton New Zealand (1958).

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: McKay: Bern Switzerland (1955).

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: Faust: San José Costa Rica (2000).

prompts.display_text: Pin a continental Western European country (not Luxembourg or a microstate) with its first stake (congregation group) 1975-82
prompts.text_original: The first European stakes, from 1960 to 1961, were in Britain, the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland. A second wave followed. One of nine continental Western European countries (Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Belgium or the Netherlands) whose first stake was organized between 1975 and 1982.
prompts.note: The Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland had stakes from 1961.
prompts.summary: After the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland received stakes in 1961, the rest of continental Western Europe waited. Paris got France's first stake in 1975, then Brussels in 1977, Vienna in 1980, Milan and Lisbon in 1981 and Madrid in 1982.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France's first stake was organized in Paris, November 16, 1975.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: The Madrid Spain Stake was organized March 14, 1982.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Italy's first stake was organized in Milan in 1981.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Ezra Taft Benson organized Austria's first stake in Vienna, April 20, 1980.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: The Brussels Belgium Stake was organized February 20, 1977.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: The Lisbon Stake was organized June 10, 1981.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land, city or region named in the Gospel of Matthew
prompts.note: Bethlehem and Jericho are in the West Bank (PSE); players may pin ISR, which is also correct for Jerusalem and Galilee.
prompts.summary: Matthew ranges well beyond Galilee. The infant Jesus was carried from Bethlehem to Egypt, his fame spread through Syria and Decapolis, and he went to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon and beyond the Jordan. Jesus cited the men of Nineveh, and Simon of Cyrene, from today's Libya, carried his cross.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem, Nazareth and Galilee run through the whole Gospel (Matthew 2:1, 22-23).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph took the young child and Mary into Egypt until Herod died (Matthew 2:14-15).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea and passed through Jericho (Matthew 2:1; 20:29).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Jesus departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: His fame went throughout all Syria, and crowds came from Decapolis (Matthew 4:24-25).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Jesus named the men of Nineveh, and the genealogy names the carrying away to Babylon (Matthew 12:41; 1:11).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Jesus came into the coasts of Judea beyond Jordan, east of the river (Matthew 19:1).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Simon, who carried the cross, was a man of Cyrene, in eastern Libya (Matthew 27:32).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that was home to a wife of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses or Boaz
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that was the homeland of a wife of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses or Boaz: Sarai from Ur, Hagar the Egyptian, Rebekah, Leah and Rachel from Laban's family at Haran, Asenath of On, Zipporah of Midian, Moses' wife from Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt, and Ruth the Moabitess
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay in today's Sudan, so modern Ethiopia is not counted.
prompts.summary: Many founding wives of Israel came from abroad. Sarai left Ur with Abram, Hagar was Egyptian, and Rebekah, Leah and Rachel came from Laban's family at Haran. Joseph married Asenath of On in Egypt, Moses married Zipporah of Midian and an Ethiopian woman, and Ruth the Moabitess became great-grandmother of David.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Hagar, Abraham's handmaid and wife, was an Egyptian; Joseph married Asenath, daughter of the priest of On (Gen 16:1-3; 41:45).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Sarai went out with Abram from Ur of the Chaldees (Gen 11:29-31); BD Ur identifies it with Mugheir near the Persian Gulf.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Boaz married Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 1:4; 4:10, 13).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Rebekah, Leah and Rachel came from the household of Laban, who lived at Haran (Gen 24:29; 27:43; 29:4-6); Church Bible Map 9 says Rebekah, Rachel, Leah, Bilhah and Zilpah came from the Haran area.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Moses dwelt in the land of Midian and married Zipporah, daughter of its priest (Ex 2:15-21); Church Bible Map 9 plots Midian east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married (Num 12:1); Bible Ethiopia was the Nile land south of Egypt.
